messages:
alice (arch): Quick RFC follow-up: we should define an explicit 'operator binding' contract between Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Without it, customers and SEs end up doing fragile env-specific hacks.
ben (platform): +1. Can you sketch what the contract covers? surface, config translation, or runtime capabilities?
alice (arch): All of the above. My thinking: a small, versioned manifest that declares supported runtime capabilities, negotiation policy (strict/best-effort/shim), and translation hints for control-plane -> operator.
clara (runtime): Important: capabilities have performance semantics. e.g. kv-cache implies warmable KV slots and consistent cache keys. quant-INT8 implies certain kernel paths. We need to make that explicit so runtime can reject or shim.
diego (ml): Also add model-related guarantees: rolling-rollout support, canary tokens, and identical model weights checksum if strict mode. Otherwise evals will diverge.
ben (platform): Sketch of config I had in mind:
```yaml
operatorBinding:
  version: "v1"
  mode: "best-effort" # strict|best-effort|shim
  capabilities:
    - kv-cache
    - quant-INT8
    - fallback-models
  translationHints:
    cachePrefix: ":tenant:cache"
    maxSeqLen: 8192
  auth: token-policy: symmetric
```
alice (arch): Exactly. Mode semantics:
- strict: fail fast if capability missing (for enterprise that needs parity)
- best-effort: try to emulate, but report degradations
- shim: provide compatibility shim at higher latency/cost
clara (runtime): Tradeoffs: strict requires same kernel selection and quantization path -> maybe only possible on Dedicated/Private. best-effort might use fallback kernels; must surface latency SLO impact.
diego (ml): We should tie mode to an eval profile: when mode != strict, run a lightweight eval set and surface drift alerts.
ben (platform): I can write a compat-linter (CLI) to validate operatorBinding manifests and emit warnings/errors based on mode/version. Want this before we expose to customers.
alice (arch): Good. We also need an on-the-wire negotiation step so control plane and operator agree at attach time. Something like:
```http
POST /negotiate HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{ "features": ["kv-cache","quant-INT8"], "version": "v1" }

-> 200 OK
{ "accepted": ["kv-cache"], "shimmed": ["quant-INT8"], "warnings": ["quant path slower"] }
```
clara (runtime): Handshake is good. Add heartbeat with capability deltas so we can detect operator upgrades/downgrades at runtime.
ben (platform): Ops question: who owns the translation layer between control-plane model config and operator manifest? Platform team or runtime team?
alice (arch): Platform owns the translator & linter. Runtime owns runtime semantics, shims, and the negotiation API surface. We'll document the boundary.
diego (ml): Action: add a canonical eval set for compatibility checks + a flag to auto-block strict-mode attach if eval fails.
ben (platform): Action: I'll prototype compat-linter and a web UI warning surface. ETA: 2w.
clara (runtime): Action: I'll prototype handshake and runtime delta heartbeat. ETA: 3w.
alice (arch): Nice. I'll draft a tiny RFC with the manifest schema, mode semantics, and migration path for v1 -> v2. Ping me for review.
sam-bot: :white_check_mark: Created task #INF-1347 'operator-binding RFC' assigned to alice (arch)
ben (platform): :thumbsup:
diego (ml): :eyes:
